The main takeaway from our work is that
, in metal-contaminated soils, the biodegradation process of metal-rich plant residues may be a source of metal release, and thus of soil contamination, when it is too slow.
the fate of metals from metal-rich plant tissues is strongly influenced by the presence of organic C in the soil, and that this effect is more marked for Cd than Zn.
the fate of metals in soil is not simply controlled by the chemical properties of the soil, but is also influenced by the chemical nature of plant residues and their decomposition.
